title: Mubayi's Question on the Triangle-Book Tradeoff
statement_text: For each $\beta \in (1/6, 1/4)$, give a more precise determination of the optimal $\gamma = \gamma(\beta) > 0$ such that every graph on $n$ vertices with at least $\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor + 1$ edges and book number at most $\beta n$ contains at least $\gamma n^3$ triangles.
context_text: Mubayi proved that for each $\beta \in (1/6, 1/4)$ there is $\gamma > 0$ such that $t(n, \beta n) \geq \gamma n^3$, and asked for a more precise determination of the optimal $\gamma$ in terms of $\beta$, noting the problem 'seems very hard'. This paper makes Conjecture 1.1 identifying the extremal graph $S_{b,n}$ as the answer and proves the conjecture for $\beta = 1/6$ and $0.2495 \leq \beta < 1/4$, thereby answering Mubayi's question in those ranges.
paper_contribution: Proposes Conjecture 1.1 as a precise answer (with extremal graph $S_{b,n}$ achieving $b^2(n-4b)$ triangles) and proves it for $b = n/6$ (Theorem 1.3) and $0.2495n \leq b < n/4$ (Theorem 1.2), fully resolving Mubayi's question in these parameter ranges.
notes: Mubayi's question is stated in prose in the introduction without a labelled theorem environment; reference is [10] in the paper's bibliography. Statement reconstructed from the paper's description.
paper_title: Books versus triangles at the extremal density

title: Conjecture 1.1
statement_text: If $n/6 \leq b < n/4$, then every graph on $n$ vertices with at least $\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$ edges and book number at most $b$ which is not the balanced complete bipartite graph has at least $b^2(n - 4b)$ triangles, with equality if and only if the graph is $S_{b,n}$.
context_text: A book of size $s$ in a graph is a set of $s$ triangles sharing a common edge, and the book number $b(G)$ is the size of the largest book, i.e. the maximum number of triangles containing a single edge. The $3$-prism graph consists of two disjoint triangles joined by a perfect matching. For $b\le n/4$, $S_{b,n}$ is the blow-up of the $3$-prism with six parts $U_1,U_2,U_3,V_1,V_2,V_3$, where $|U_1|=|U_2|=|V_1|=|V_2|=b$, $|U_3|=\lfloor(n-4b)/2\rfloor$, $|V_3|=\lceil(n-4b)/2\rceil$, $U_i$ is complete to $U_j$ and $V_i$ to $V_j$ for $i\ne j$, $U_i$ is complete to $V_i$ for each $i$, and there are no other edges; it has $n$ vertices, $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ edges, $b^2(n-4b)$ triangles, and book number $b$ when $b\ge n/6$. By Mantel and Rademacher, graphs with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+1$ edges have at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ triangles, and by Edwards and Khadžiivanov–Nikiforov they have book number at least $n/6$. Mubayi asked for the minimum number $t(n,b)$ of triangles in a graph on $n$ vertices with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+1$ edges and book number at most $b$; he showed that for each $\beta\in(1/6,1/4)$ there is $\gamma>0$ with $t(n,\beta n)\ge\gamma n^3$, and asked for the optimal $\gamma(\beta)$. This conjecture (which allows $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ edges instead) would imply an asymptotically tight bound on $t(n,b)$ for $n/6\le b\le n/4-\omega(1)$, answering Mubayi's question; an almost identical construction appeared in the original arXiv version of Mubayi's paper. The authors prove the conjecture, for graphs with at least $n^2/4$ edges, when $0.2495n\le b<n/4$ and when $b=n/6$.
paper_title: Books versus triangles at the extremal density
